This confirms it exactly: commit `b12a8a63` removed the `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader);` call entirely, apparently assuming the two-arg constructor `(Mode.class, ClassLoader.class)` would handle setting the classloader internally (a constructor that, per the full history of `Workflow.java` and `workflow2class.egl`, never actually existed/set the serializer's classloader). Commit `a6b23429` reverted the constructor call back to the single-arg form (likely fixing a `NoSuchMethodException`), but never restored the `setClassloader` call, leaving the underlying serializer-classloader bug intact. `f5c417c7` finally restores that missing call.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b12a8a63db38dcdb3b93503fe9f3552bc341a87d

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the file history of `CrossflowHandler.java` and found that the fix commit (`f5c417c7`) re-adds a single line, `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader);`, right after the workflow instance is constructed via reflection. I used `git log -p` on this file to see every historical version of that block, and also checked `git log -p` on `Serializer.java` and `Workflow.java`/`workflow2class.egl` (the Epsilon template that generates each experiment's `Workflow` subclass) to understand when/why the classloader was or wasn't propagated to the XStream serializer.

(2) The line was first introduced in `1849376f` and persisted unchanged through many commits. In `b12a8a63` ("big refactor" touching `CrossflowHandler.java`/`UploadExperiment.java`), the author rewrote the `startExperiment` method and, instead of calling `.getConstructor(Mode.class)` + `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader)`, switched to `.getConstructor(Mode.class, ClassLoader.class).newInstance(mode, classLoader)` and **dropped the `setClassloader` call**. However, I confirmed via `git log -p` across the entire history of `Workflow.java` and `workflow2class.egl` that no `Workflow(Mode, ClassLoader)` constructor ever existed anywhere in the codebase — the generated workflow classes only ever have `Workflow(Mode)` and `Workflow(Mode, int)` constructors. So this two-arg constructor call was itself broken, and crucially, the mechanism for giving the serializer's XStream instance the correct classloader was lost.

(3) Commit `a6b23429` (two days later) changed the constructor call back to `.getConstructor(Mode.class).newInstance(mode)` — fixing the `NoSuchMethodException`/reflection failure — but it did **not** restore the `setClassloader` line that `b12a8a63` had deleted. This left the workflow's serializer without the correct classloader (causing it to use the default/non-experiment classloader, which would likely break XStream deserialization of experiment-specific classes). The bug-fixing commit `f5c417c7` simply re-adds that exact line back, in the exact same position it originally occupied before `b12a8a63` removed it.

I'm confident in `b12a8a63` as the bug-introducing commit, since it's the exact point where the `setClassloader` call was deleted and no subsequent commit restored it until the fix. `a6b23429` is a related, intermediate commit that fixed a different symptom (the invalid constructor signature) but did not reintroduce the missing call, so it's not itself the root cause, just a commit in between that left the bug latent in a different form.
